page: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. For high-capacity local storage, it bundles 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 56 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7i.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier performance across multi-threaded and data-intensive operations. Multi-core CPU performance is rated as strong, while Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores place the server in the top 10% tier. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers strong read and write bandwidth, particularly in large-block uncached operations. Database and memory-bound operations are highly efficient, with Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations achieving top-tier ratings, the latter reaching 122.39 million operations per second. The server also exhibits strong performance in LLM inference tasks, particularly for prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds for larger models remain moderate.

The hardware profile of the i7i.metal-24xl offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-throughput local storage and substantial memory capacity without the overhead of virtualization. The absence of a GPU makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, but its AMX instruction support enables efficient CPU-based inference. This server is optimized for large-scale databases, high-performance computing, software compilation, and intensive data processing tasks.
